steps.body: Two triangles are **similar** if just TWO pairs of their angles match. Since all three angles of any triangle sum to 180°, matching two forces the third to match too — so the triangles have the same shape. This is the **angle-angle (AA)** rule.

predict.prompt: Both triangles have angles of 50° and 60°. Their THIRD angles…
predict.reveal: Each third angle is 180 − 110 = 70 — forced on both. Three matching angles means the same SHAPE: similar. Size stays free, and that freedom is exactly the gap between similar and congruent.

steps.body: Why does two force the third? Because the three must total 180°. If two triangles share two angles, their third angles are both 180 minus the same sum — so those match automatically. Equal angles mean the same shape.

explanationVariants: Both triangles have 40° and 75°, so both have a third of 180 − 40 − 75 = 65° — similar.
